title: Pre-Analysis — Trim Air Zone Regulation Standard 2, Second Round for the Duct Boss Finding
abstract: Second round of pre-analysis on the standard 2 regulation, opened after the duct boss weld toe crack findings, to establish what the released standard obliges the fleet to do while a third standard is studied.

sections.objective: Twenty-nine crack findings at the duct boss weld toe across the modified population reopened the analysis on a modification that had been in service for six years. The round was not asked whether the modification was correct; it was asked what the released standard now obliges operators to do, which of its published content becomes invalid if the boss is eventually deleted, and how much of that content can be written once rather than twice.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. The conversion bulletin and its kit are the vehicle for every boss weld in the fleet and its accomplishment instructions are the only place the boss alignment is controlled, so any change to the boss standard lands there first. The installation task in the maintenance manual sets the clamp torque sequence against the boss position and would need re-issue in step with it. The trouble shooting procedure for an unresponsive zone leans on the boss sensor as the primary measurement, and on a boss-less standard its first three steps would be meaningless. The fourth finding is the candidate third standard itself, which deletes the boss entirely and supersedes this modification; the round recommended that the maintenance content be re-issued once, against the third standard, rather than twice.
sections.next_steps: Hold the publication change requests for the installation task and the trouble shooting procedure until the third standard clears its own pre-analysis, and issue them together. Keep the boss weld inspection as a repeat item on the modified population until then. Pass the boss alignment control question to the third standard's review rather than answering it here.

similarity_seeds: weld toe cracking at a boss welded into a pressurised duct flange
publication content that assumes a duct mounted sensing element

tasks.title: Map the published content that depends on the duct boss
Assess the sequencing against the candidate third standard
Confirm the boss weld inspection interval with in-service engineering

expected_findings.rationale: The conversion bulletin is the vehicle for every boss weld in the fleet and its accomplishment instructions are the only place the boss alignment is controlled. Any change to the boss standard lands here first.
expected_findings.resolution: Hold a revision of the bulletin until the third standard position is known.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task sets the clamp torque sequence against the boss position, so it must be re-issued in step with any change to the boss standard.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise the publication change request but hold it for issue with the third standard.

expected_findings.rationale: The trouble shooting procedure treats the duct boss sensor as the primary measurement. On a boss-less standard its first three steps are meaningless.
expected_findings.resolution: Rewrite the first three steps when the third standard is released.

expected_findings.rationale: The candidate third standard deletes the duct boss entirely and supersedes this modification. Re-issuing the maintenance content now would mean writing it twice.
expected_findings.resolution: Sequence all publication changes behind the third standard's own pre-analysis.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by the similarity search on wording about a hot air duct joint inspection, but it is the air cycle machine inspection on a different chapter and it does not touch the trim air distribution run or any boss weld.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a clear sequencing recommendation. The published content that depends on the duct boss was mapped and held for a single re-issue against the third standard rather than being revised twice.
